notes: Synthetic procurement fixture. Entity → Organization → Company → Supplier is the inheritance example locked by INF-606. Distractor skills for the RAG/dump-all control live in skills_distractors.json and must not attach to Company / Organization / Entity.

skills.title: Identity hygiene
skills.body: Mint one entity URI per real-world individual. Never invent a second URI because a name string differs in case, punctuation, or legal suffix (Ltd, Inc, GmbH). Carry aliases as literals, not as extra nodes.

skills.title: Legal name normalization
skills.body: Store legalName as the registry form. Collapse whitespace. Preserve Inc/Ltd/GmbH as part of legalName. Trade names go on alias, never overwrite legalName from a nickname.

skills.title: Company registration id
skills.body: Map VAT, EIN, company-number, and 'registration no' columns onto registrationId. Treat registrationId as a unique key for entity resolution when present. Do not put a registration id on a Person.

skills.title: Supplier vendor reconciliation
skills.body: A Supplier is a Company that sells to a Customer. Require vendorId or registrationId. Incoterms and payment terms are literals on the Supplier, not on the supplied Product. Do not type a buying organization as Supplier.

skills.title: SUPPLIES_TO temporal window
skills.body: SUPPLIES_TO is a temporally qualified edge. If the source row has valid_from / valid_to, write them as edge literals. Two invoices in the same window are one edge, not two. Do not emit SUPPLIES_TO without a typed Supplier source and Customer target.

skills.title: SUPPLIES_TO quantity validation
skills.body: Quantity and currency must be non-negative. Reject or repair rows where qty < 0. A missing qty is allowed; a negative qty is a constraint violation.

skills.title: Person is not an Organization
skills.body: A Person must not be the source of SUPPLIES_TO. If a vendor row names a human, type them Person and attach EMPLOYS from the Supplier; do not coerce the Person into Supplier.
